LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N005Care_Text: These past few days, someone has always had to put down their work to care for the children. At least now, every cry no longer starts with asking whom to call.\n\nTheir old names remain. Whether to change them is up to you.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N005Dead_Text: The children did not survive. That trade was paid in full. Nobody will come back to refund anything.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N005Left_Text: The children have left your care. How they will be looked after elsewhere is not yet known.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N005Missing_Text: Some time has passed since the handover, with no news that the children have settled in. Suin has written to ask how they are doing.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_BroadcastEcho_Text: "The broadcast is still going out. Those who hear it will not know why the gate is closed today."
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N008Entry_Text:
"I came to ask for those of us still alive."

{0} grips the hem of their clothes and pauses before continuing.

"We need food. I know an old store. Give me six simple meals and I will tell you where it is. You can check my story first. I can wait here for three days."
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N008Verified_Text: "That part matches. I cannot promise the rest, and you need not believe me yet."\n\nThe visitor's account matches something in your records. The offer still stands.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N008Unverified_Text: There is no past event here to match the account.\n\n"Perhaps I came to the wrong place." The visitor does not insist.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N008Traded_Text: "Enough. Don't bring any more. I cannot carry it all alone."\n\nThe visitor handed over the promised location and checked the route home once more.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N008Rejected_Text: "Then never mind. I still have to get out before dark."\n\nThe visitor gathers their things and prepares to leave.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N008Dead_Text: The envoy has died, leaving the message unfinished.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N008Missing_Text: The envoy can no longer be found at the meeting place. The unfinished exchange has fallen through.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N008Left_Text: The envoy has left the meeting. The offer has been withdrawn.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N008Timeout_Text: Three days have passed. The envoy has stopped waiting. Supplies not yet handed over remain in the colony.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N008ExtraSite: The visitor marked another place on the map. What remains there is anyone's guess.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N009Entry_Text: The visitor pointed out an old store on the map, said to hold lists left during the migration.\n\n"Someone is coming to clear the place out. If you mean to go, get there within fifteen days."
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N009Result1_Text: Everything that can be carried has been packed. A few pages are stuck together. Do not pull them apart yet.\n\nThe records and silver are beside the chest. Remember to collect them.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N009Result2_Label: Leave it for those who follow
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N009Result2_Text: You did not take the chest. The location has been noted, but what the next visitors do with it is no longer yours to decide.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N009Result3_Text: You handed the records to the people contacted earlier. They left the agreed silver and carefully wrapped the old papers.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N009Result4_Text: "Leave us a copy. Once you take it away, don't make us ask you again."\n\nThe arrangement is settled. Your copy is at the site. There is no silver payment this time.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N009Result5_Text: The paper and wooden chest are beyond use. There is no other copy here to check the names against.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N009Result6_Text: When you asked about the cellar again, nobody could be found to lead the way. The trail has gone cold.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N007Return_Text: A familiar face is at the gate again. The Ratkin plague had cleared before they left last time.\n\nThis time, they ask only for a meal and a chance to share news of a shorter route. You can welcome them or let them continue. They will wait one day.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_N007ReturnReceived_T: Two meals have been handed over. The visitor is preparing to leave again, with no further requests.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_E01_Text:
As the final act of aid was entered in the ledger, Suin wrote a name in the margin. Halfway through, she stopped for a long time.

"I once promised to take her child somewhere there would be food. That time, I failed. Ever since, I have looked for that child on every list that reached me. I never found them."

The next page lists food sent, patients tended and visitors allowed to leave.

"There are many people here whom I have never met. You helped them keep living. I should say that properly, at least once."

"Thank you. And to the children growing up there: eat your meals without fear. Someone has already set aside your share."

Aid completed: {0}. Successful broadcasts: {1}. The famine is not over, but this colony has become somewhere people can reach.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_E02_Text:
This year's roll lists {2} adult famine Ratkin in one colony. Suin had to add several pages. Children who once trailed behind the crowd can now sign beside their own names.

"When I used to ask where they were going, the answer was often: a little farther."

"Now some give the name of your colony. Some count the days of the return journey; some ask a visitor to carry a message. Someone will be waiting for them."

She enclosed the first crumpled plea for help.

"Keep this for me. I have a copy. The original belongs where they live."

"You still have many years to share. Houses will age, people will argue, and harvests will be good or bad. When they grow old and speak of this year, I hope someone beside them will remember it too."
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_E03_Text:
Suin sent an account of the past months. It lists dates when food arrived, and blank spaces where nothing was heard after a group left.

"This is as far as I can confirm. I am still looking for where the people who left alive went, and whether those who could not stay found somewhere else."

"Sometimes you reached out. Sometimes the gate stayed closed. I recorded both. From so far away, I cannot know how much food was left inside that day."

A blank reply slip is enclosed.

"If you hear anything, send it to me. Even a single name. I would like to fill these spaces, little by little."

The record closes for now. The colony carries on, and new visitors may still appear on the road.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_E04_Text:
This time, Suin did not ask how you were. She returned several pages, marking the most troubling entries.

"I have read them and checked them. You may have your reasons. Those people have already borne the consequences."

"I cannot keep writing beside the pleas for help: try going here. Someone will believe those words and take their children onto the road."

She still left a return address.

"I hope those already entrusted to you will still be cared for. I will keep watching what happens. But I cannot offer you my trust now."

The address is unchanged. The voice of the letters is not.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_E05_Text:
The letter is short, with a clear signature.

"I will no longer vouch for this place. I will give the records of what happened to those affected."

"Someone asked why I trusted you in the first place. I must answer them in person."

"Those who remain with you still need food, treatment and sleep. I will send no more idle news, but their lives go on. Necessary handovers and reports will still reach you."

"Suin."

No new pleas for help are enclosed. She asks for no reply. Others will continue reading those records.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_PublicEnding_Text: The aid given over these months now fills a register. Some found food along the road; others made a home here.\n\nAid given: {0}. Broadcasts sent: {1}. At the last count, one settlement was home to {2} adult famine Ratkin.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_IdentityEntry_Text: "I know some old storehouse numbers, and I can reach people who arrange transport.\n\nI have not explained that properly before. We can talk about it now."
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_IdentityFull_Text:
"I am a princess of the kingdom. My name really is Suin. I have never changed it.

I know there are still so many people begging outside. I keep asking those who can afford to leave grain in their stores.

This money is what I can spare. The transport, too. I do not have an army that can open every road.

Now you know. Do not start addressing me differently because of a title. I have not done enough to deserve that."
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_IdentityPartial_Text: "I used to keep some accounts for the kingdom, and I can contact a few people who arrange transport. There are other things I do not wish to say yet.\n\nOnce spoken, they cannot be unsaid. That is enough for today."
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_BridgeChild_Text: "Once again, someone is deciding where the children will go. What happened last time cannot make this decision for you."
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_BridgeGrain_Text: "There is another place along that food route. Whether the two are connected, someone will have to go and see."
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_BridgePlague_Text: "News can travel only when someone survives to carry it. This visitor has not mentioned the quarantine."
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_BridgeEnvoy_Text: "The place they spoke of has been found. This time, at least, the promised lead went somewhere."
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S12Paid_Text: After handing over the supplies, the caravan was allowed to continue. The remaining food will need to stretch further.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S12Fight_Text: The caravan refused to surrender its supplies. Its members set down their packs and took up their weapons.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S01_Label: Children sent to the wrong place
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S01_Text: At first, it was a mistaken destination. Once the pod opened, someone still had to decide where the children would go.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S02_Text: The visitor who mistook you for someone else is already here. The mistake can be corrected. Their future needs a separate answer.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S03_Text: There is another child on the road. Among the mother's few belongings, room must be found for a swaddling cloth.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S04_Text: There is news of where this group went. Some visitors pass through only once.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S05_Text: The grain sacks still bear signs of being searched. Some count what remains; others ask after the visitors.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S06_Text: News becomes confused when there are so many people. This time, at least some of their fates are known.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S07_Text: The visitors' account placed a food cache only roughly on the map. Their description of the hills and waterways was much more precise.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S08_Text: The caravan left behind a few trades and news of some of its people. A few more lines fill the ledger by the counter.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S09_Text: The wall is quiet again. The guards change shifts while someone goes out to inspect the traces left by the visitors.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S10_Text: News of the group has come back in fragments. Suin gathers the scraps and checks the names one by one.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S11_Text: The visitors were infected. A claim of revenge is not proof of who sent them. Names not yet found remain blank.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S12_Text: News has arrived from the caravan. Its members spoke of the people who blocked the road and counted their remaining supplies.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S13_Text: They arrived alone, without even a companion to carry a message. It took Suin several inquiries to piece together their journey.
LanguageData.MouseDisaster_Story_S14_Text: News of the visitors seeking help has arrived. Suin recognized the names: this was the group that had sent someone to ask the way.
